subject: Clarifications: model catalog licensing, provenance & version-pinning for RFI
messages:
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@finservcorp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: FinServCorp Procurement <procurement@finservcorp.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifications on model catalog licensing and version pinning for RFI

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the RFI packet — the model catalog section is very helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our security and procurement teams around licensing and provenance before we proceed:

1) License lineage: for open-source models you list license types (Apache-2.0, MIT, etc.). Can you confirm whether Redwood stores a per-model license text and that you give us an explicit statement on derivative/fine-tuning rights for each catalog entry? We need an auditable record.

2) Provenance metadata: do you provide immutable checksums (SHA256) for every model weight file in the catalog and a timestamped record of when a catalog entry was published/updated? We need to map models to our internal SBOM process.

3) Version pinning and update policy: if a model in the catalog receives a patch (bug/security or improved weights), what is your recommended approach for long-lived production deployments? Do you provide a pinned-hash artifact and a notification window prior to automatic rollouts?

4) Export/redistribution: if we fine-tune a model served via Redwood Dedicated, are there any licensing or export limitations we should be aware of?

We want concise written answers we can include in our RFP response appendix (short paragraphs plus any artifact or link). Can you route to whoever owns licensing/provenance docs?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Nguyen
Senior Security Program Manager
FinServCorp

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Clarifications on model catalog licensing and version pinning for RFI

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear questions. Replying inline with attachments and a brief implementation note: I copied Legal (Priyom) and Research (Jonas) for provenance artifacts.

1) License lineage
- Short answer: yes. For every catalog entry Redwood stores the canonical license text and a provenance record linking to the original upstream artifact (model repo or release URL) where the license was published. We attach an explicit human-readable summary for business reviewers that lists whether the license permits modification, commercial use, and redistribution.
- Implementation note: see attachment Model_Catalog_License_Appendix_v3.pdf (page 2 summarizes rights-by-license).

2) Provenance metadata
- We publish an immutable checksum for each model weight file (SHA256) and a signed manifest (PKCS7) that includes: checksum, artifact size, originating source URL (when available), publish timestamp, Redwood catalog version, and a build/hash ID. The catalog UI surfaces these and they can be exported as CSV (see Model_Hash_Checksums_202605.csv).
- We also keep an audit trail of catalog events (created/updated/deprecated) with timestamps and actor ids (service account or human username) for compliance.

3) Version pinning and update policy
- Redwood supports explicit model pinning by model-name + semantic version + immutable hash. Customers can pin to a specific hash. By default Hosted runs on a stable release channel; Dedicated customers can choose: 
  * pinned-hash (no auto-updates)
  * pinned-major (minor/patch auto-updates within a major)
  * latest (automatic updates)
- Update policy: we never silently change a pinned-hash. For non-pinned channels we provide a 30-day notification window for non-critical upgrades and a 72-hour notification for critical security fixes; in emergencies we will provide a gravity-driven rollback strategy and a compatibility matrix.

4) Export/redistribution for fine-tuning
- Licensing: if the underlying model license permits redistribution/modification (e.g., Apache-2.0, MIT) then fine-tuning and redistribution of resulting weights are allowed subject to that license. If a model is under a restrictive license (e.g., some custom CC variants or models with data-use restrictions), that will be clearly flagged in the catalog entry.
- Operational note: for Redwood Dedicated/Private deployments, customers host the model weights in their VPC or on-prem storage; we do not add additional redistribution restrictions beyond the upstream license and the customer’s own terms. Priyom: please see the draft legal wording below that we recommend customers use in procurements.

Attachments: Model_Catalog_License_Appendix_v3.pdf, Model_Hash_Checksums_202605.csv

Next steps: If this level of detail works, we can produce a short attestation (DocuSign) that you can attach to the RFP appendix. Happy to provide a CSV export of the catalog rows referenced in your RFI.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarifications on model catalog licensing and version pinning for RFI

Karthik — quick legal clarifications and an editable paragraph we should send to FinServCorp as formal language for the RFI appendix. Please review:

Legal clarifications (high level):
- We provide the canonical upstream license text and a Redwood catalog summary that states permitted actions (modify, distribute, commercial use). These summaries are intended for reviewer convenience and do not replace the upstream license text.
- Where upstream licensing is ambiguous or where model training data imposes additional use restrictions, the catalog entry is flagged as "restricted" and Redwood will surface the original source and any documented restrictions.
- For customers who require a written attestation, Redwood can sign a limited attestation that the catalog snapshots and checksums provided correspond to the artifacts we served at the stated timestamps. This is not a license grant; it is an operational attestation for provenance and integrity.

Suggested RFI appendix paragraph (editable):
"Redwood Inference maintains a model catalog with per-artifact metadata that includes the canonical upstream license text, an operational summary of permitted actions (modification, commercial use, redistribution), and immutable SHA256 checksums for each published model weight file. Customers may pin any deployment to an immutable model hash; Redwood will not modify pinned hashes without explicit customer authorization. For customers requiring formal provenance documentation, Redwood can provide timestamped signed manifests and an attestation of the catalog snapshot delivered to the customer."

Marissa — happy to fold in any commercial caveats (credits, support) if you want alternative phrasing. Jonas — please confirm the manifest signing format/keys are noted correctly (we referenced PKCS7 in the sales reply).

-Priyom
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
